title: Why You Can Feel Pain From a Missing Limb
hook: Feeling pain in a limb that isn't there?

narration.text: Your brain can make you feel pain from a limb that has been amputated.
This is called phantom limb syndrome. It is very real.
Your brain has a map of your entire body. Each part is represented.
When a limb is removed, the brain area for it does not disappear.
Instead, nearby brain areas can remap and invade that space.
This remapping can cause confused signals, leading to pain.
It shows how powerful and adaptable your brain truly is.
Have you heard of anyone experiencing phantom sensations?

description: Discover why some people experience pain from an amputated limb, a phenomenon known as phantom limb syndrome. Learn how the brain's incredible ability to remap itself can lead to these vivid and often distressing sensations. This video explains the fascinating science behind your brain's body map.
topic: Why you can feel pain from a limb that has been amputated, explaining phantom limb syndrome and brain remapping.
